survey: Image 4 is a stylized ringed planet (a Saturn-like toy) on a purple striped background. Main parts: (1) The orange sphere, shaded as one ball with its light from the upper left. (2) A thick cream band around its upper half. It runs at the same tilt as the ring, rising to the right. It sags toward the viewer in the middle and wraps out of sight at the upper right, which is how a latitude band looks from slightly above. (3) Below the ring, a second cream band and orange bands peek out. They also follow the ring's tilt and wrap up the right edge of the sphere. (4) A blue porthole with an orange rim sits on the upper band near the left edge of the sphere. Because that part of the sphere curves away from the viewer, it is drawn as a slightly narrowed upright oval. (5) The flat yellow ring is a wide open ellipse, low on the left and high on the right. We see its top surface and a thin front edge, so the camera is slightly above the ring's plane. The ring's hole is centred on the sphere. Its front passes in front of the lower half of the sphere and its back passes behind the upper half. Purple background shows through the hole on both sides where the sphere does not fill it. The object floats, so there is no ground contact to check. The ring, the bands and the porthole all agree on one slightly-above viewpoint and one tilt.
